items.stem: Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from (−1, −3) to the line −x + y = 0, and the image of the point in the line.
items.markingKey: The perpendicular through the point has direction (−1, 1) (1); write (x, y) = (−1, −3) + t(−1, 1) and substitute in the line (1); t = 1 gives the foot (−2, −2) (1); the image is at twice the distance: (−3, −1) (1).

items.stem: Find the point of intersection of the lines 4x + 4y − 20 = 0 and 2x + 5y − 22 = 0.
items.markingKey: Solve the two equations simultaneously (elimination) (1): x = 1, y = 4 (1).

items.stem: A firm's cost function is C(x) = 40x + 8000 and it sells each unit at ₹80. Find the break-even point. What is the profit when 250 units are sold?
A line has slope 1/2. Find the slope of a line perpendicular to it.
items.markingKey: Perpendicular lines have m₁m₂ = −1: −2.

items.stem: A machine costs ₹3,00,000 and has a scrap value of ₹30,000 after 8 years. Using straight-line depreciation, write the value V as a linear function of time t (years) and find the value after 7 years.
Which of the following statements about the general equation of a line is NOT correct?
items.markingKey: (a) "Lines 2x + 3y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 5 are parallel." is false; the other three are true.
options: Lines 2x + 3y = 5 and 3x + 2y = 5 are parallel.
Lines A₁x + B₁y + C₁ = 0 and A₂x + B₂y + C₂ = 0 are parallel if A₁/A₂ = B₁/B₂ ≠ C₁/C₂.
The y-intercept of Ax + By + C = 0 is −C/B.
Every first-degree equation Ax + By + C = 0 (A, B not both zero) represents a straight line.

items.stem: Find the value of k for which the lines 3x + y − 1 = 0, −2x + 2y + 6 = 0 and kx + y + 5 = 0 are concurrent.
items.markingKey: The first two lines meet at (1, −2) (2); this point lies on the third line: 1k + (−2) + (5) = 0 (1) ⇒ k = −3 (1).

items.stem:
Assertion (A): The lines y = 5x + 1 and y = 5x − 6 are parallel.
Reason (R): Non-vertical lines are parallel if and only if their slopes are equal.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
items.markingKey: (a) Both slopes are 5; R explains A.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

items.stem: Find the perpendicular distance of the point (−3, 3) from the line −12x + 5y + 3 = 0.

Assertion (A): The lines y = 5x + 1 and y = 1/5x − 3 are perpendicular.
Reason (R): Two non-vertical lines are perpendicular if the product of their slopes is −1.
Choose the correct option.
items.answer: A is false, but R is true.
items.markingKey: (d) A is false: 5 × 1/5 = 1, not −1. R is true.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.

items.stem: Find the equation of the line through (−1, 6) and (3, 5).

The demand for a product is 0 when the price is ₹100 and 15 units when the price is ₹70; the supply function is p = 15 + 3q. Assuming linear demand, find the demand function and the equilibrium price and quantity.
items.markingKey: Demand line through (0, 100) and (15, 70): slope −2, p = 100 − 2q (2). Equate with supply: 100 − 2q = 15 + 3q ⇒ q = 17 (2), p = 66 (1).

items.stem:
An auto-rickshaw in Patna charges ₹98 for a 3 km ride and ₹210 for a 10 km ride. The fare y (₹) is a linear function of the distance x (km).
(i) Find the slope of the fare line and interpret it. (ii) Write the equation of the line. (iii) What is the fare for 15 km? (iv) What does the y-intercept represent?
items.answer: (i) 16, the charge per km (₹16/km) (ii) y = 16x + 50 (iii) ₹290 (iv) the fixed (minimum) charge ₹50
items.markingKey: (i) (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁) (1). (ii) two-point form (1). (iii) substitute x (1). (iv) value at x = 0 (1).

items.stem: Using slopes, check whether the points A(4, 4), B(7, 10) and C(8, 12) are collinear. Explain your reasoning.
items.answer: slope AB = 2, slope BC = 2; equal, so A, B, C are collinear.
items.markingKey: Both slopes (1); conclusion with reason that equal slopes through a common point B give one line (1).

items.stem:
On a district map (1 unit = 1 km), the new highway is the line 6x + 8y − 52 = 0 and the village Chandanpur is at (1, 1). A straight link road is to be built from Chandanpur to the highway.
(i) What should be the direction of the link road for it to be shortest? (ii) Find the length of the shortest link road. (iii) If the road costs ₹5 lakh per km, find the cost. (iv) Find the slope of the link road.
items.answer: (i) perpendicular to the highway (ii) 19/5 km (iii) ₹19 lakh (iv) 4/3
items.markingKey: (i) Shortest distance is along the perpendicular (1). (ii) |Ax₀ + By₀ + C|/√(A² + B²) (1). (iii) length × rate (1). (iv) negative reciprocal of −3/4 (1).

items.stem: Find the equation of the line through (2, −4) that is perpendicular to −5x + 3y + 2 = 0.
items.markingKey: A perpendicular line has the form Bx − Ay + k = 0 (1); substitute (2, −4) to find k (1): 3x + 5y + 14 = 0 (1).

items.stem: A line has slope −2. Find the slope of a line parallel to it.
items.markingKey: Parallel lines have equal slopes: −2.

items.stem: Find the equation of the line with x-intercept −2 and y-intercept 5.
Find the coordinates of the foot of the perpendicular from (8, −3) to the line −12x + 5y − 58 = 0, and the image of the point in the line.
items.markingKey: The perpendicular through the point has direction (−12, 5) (1); write (x, y) = (8, −3) + t(−12, 5) and substitute in the line (1); t = 1 gives the foot (−4, 2) (1); the image is at twice the distance: (−16, 7) (1).
